context: 2D density contour heatmap of 8,000 points from 3 bivariate normal clusters with brush-to-zoom interactivity; contours rendered via d3.contourDensity over a canvas scatter layer
first_impression: Structurally honest scatter+density hybrid with data-driven domains and correct zoom-recompute, but fixed bandwidth and color-scale renormalization on zoom silently change encoding meaning across views.
what_works: X/Y domains derived from d3.extent with proportional padding — no hardcoded magic numbers; contour color scale domain recalculated from current contours' max density, keeping color meaningful within each view.
what_doesnt: Bandwidth hardcoded at 25px regardless of data spread (should use Silverman's rule or be data-driven); color scale renormalizes on every brush-zoom so the same viridis yellow means different absolute densities before vs. after zoom, breaking cross-view comparison without any legend or warning.
